notes: Experimental Sepolia testnet project; this manifest describes the accepted sources and preserves unresolved findings for independent review. LaunchToken has no constructor arguments. JackpotVault opens at a 3% reserve payout with a 600-second cooldown; CharityVault opens at a 1% reserve donation with a 3600-second cooldown. All administrator and owner arguments resolve exclusively through policy via $owner. BLOCKING BENEFICIARY FINDING: CharityVault's second argument currently resolves to $owner as an unapproved provisional donation recipient. The approved brief does not identify a charity. Policy ownership alone does not authorize receiving charity donations; this argument needs explicit beneficiary authorization or replacement with an approved nonzero recipient before admission. BLOCKING POOL FINDING: pool describes the permitted native-ETH factory launch pool. HauntedHook.afterInitialize requires the dynamic-fee flag 0x800000 and the game requires swap callbacks, whereas this manifest permits only fee 3000 and the factory supplies an initialization-only PoolInitializationGuard. Listing HauntedHook does not attach it to the launch pool. The accepted code therefore does not deliver the requested haunted dynamic-fee launch pool under this policy; a separate pool would require a separately approved integration and liquidity plan. BLOCKING CONSTRUCTOR CONFIGURATION FINDING: vault constructors grant only administrator and pauser roles. HauntedHook receives neither JackpotVault.PAYER_ROLE nor CharityVault.SIGNALER_ROLE; its payout and donation attempts are skipped without those permissions. The accepted implementation requires subsequent role grants, conflicting with complete constructor configuration. No initialization calls are encoded or authorized here. HOOK ADDRESS FINDING: HauntedHook's constructor reverts unless its address masked by 0x3fff equals 0x10c0. A compatible CREATE2 salt must be proven using the actual factory, resolved arguments and creation bytecode; manifest syntax and local salt mining do not establish deployer support. The PoolManager argument is the Sepolia address listed at https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v4/deployments#sepolia-11155111; service network/policy compatibility still needs review. The contracts do not restrict owner test controls to Sepolia, so the deployment chain must be enforced by service policy. Notes do not authorize a beneficiary, policy change or extra deployment. Publication, signed artifact linkage, independent review, admission, deployment and frontend activation remain service responsibilities; none is claimed complete.
